asDecan.p: Your Sun sits in the last ten degrees of Aries, somewhere between 20 and 29, and in the old Chaldean order that slice of the sign is given to Venus. Every sign is split into thirds like this, each with its own planet and its own small card. Early Aries belongs to Mars and the Two of Wands, the sign at its most raw. The middle goes to the Sun and the Three of Wands, where the fire gets some confidence and starts looking out at the horizon. Then comes Venus, and the Four of Wands, the one with a garland strung across four staves and people holding flowers up in front of a big house. Venus is the planet of liking and being liked, of company and pleasure. She's in detriment in Aries, because Aries sits opposite Libra, one of her own signs, so she's made to work at Mars's speed, and you can usually see her working. Your Sun card is still The Emperor, and this one sits inside it.

You start things like any Aries, fast and a bit before you're ready, but you rarely want to start them alone. The new job is barely a week old and you've already worked out who you'll get lunch with. When a friend gets engaged you're the one who books the table, sends the group message and rings the restaurant twice to check they've got the cake. A Sunday with nothing planned lasts until about eleven, and then you're texting three people to see who's around. People who meet you at a party might guess you're a Libra or a Leo. They find out otherwise the first time somebody talks over you in a meeting. The Mars underneath is very much there, and you'll say so, in front of everyone, in a perfectly pleasant voice.

Charm is the obvious one, and it's real, but the more useful thing I see with this decan is that you're good at repair. Aries picks fights. Venus hates leaving them unfinished. Get both in one person and you have someone who can have a proper row with a colleague at ten and be sitting with them at lunch by one, and mean it. You don't sulk for a week, and nobody has to grovel. There's also some Taurus leaking in at this end of the sign, since the last ten degrees are already leaning toward the next one, and it gives you something the earlier Aries degrees mostly lack, which is the patience to stay and enjoy a thing once it's built. The garden you dug gets sat in. Family Christmas after a hard year tends to go better when you're the one running it, to be honest.

A Venus in detriment tends to overdo it, the way anyone does with something that doesn't come easily, and with you that usually means trying too hard to make everyone happy at once, then getting hurt when nobody notices. You organised the whole weekend away. Two people dropped out on the Thursday. You said it was fine, it wasn't, and eight months later you're still slightly cool with one of them. There's a scorekeeping side to this decan that people don't expect from someone so warm. The other version is jumping to the milestone too early, calling something a win or a relationship before it's really either, because you love the feeling of arriving and Aries hates waiting for anything. You buy the champagne after the first-round interview. Then you have to explain it to everyone who asks how it went.

When something goes wrong, your first move is Aries through and through. You do something. The breakup happens on a Friday and by Saturday night you've got six people at the pub and you're telling it as a funny story. Grief gets turned into organising, the funeral, the food, the list of who's bringing what. About a week later it catches up, and it usually comes out sideways as irritation with whoever's closest, the partner who stacked the dishwasher wrong, the sister who didn't ring back. The people around you often feel they're being hosted through your bad patch instead of let into it. What actually helps is the part Venus struggles with in Aries, which is being looked after. One person, a couch, food you didn't cook, and nobody you have to be good company for.

You don't hide interest well and you don't really try. If you like someone they know within the week, usually because you've asked them out yourself. What surprises people is how quickly it turns domestic. Two months in you want to meet their friends, you want them at your mum's birthday, you'd quite like a key. Some partners love that. The slower ones feel rushed, and this Venus tends to read slowness as a no and push harder, which only makes it more of a no. The odd part is that being chased can put you off. Someone who turns up with flowers before you've made your move may find you've gone a bit cool, and you don't always know why yourself. That's Mars wanting to go first. The partners who last usually let you set the pace early, then quietly start setting some of it a year or so in.

At work you're the one who notices when a team has quietly hit something and nobody's said so. When the release finally goes live you order the pizzas and make a short speech that names everyone who stayed late. That makes you very good anywhere with a launch, an opening night, a deadline everyone is running at together, so events, hospitality, sales, a small company in its first few years. The Emperor is still over all of this, so you want to run things eventually, and you usually do. The trouble is the long flat middle of a project, the maintenance months after the ribbon's been cut, when there's nothing to mark. You drift then, and start reading job ads at your desk. It also stings more than you let on when a year of work goes by without anyone above you saying well done.

At twenty this decan mostly looks like a very social Aries. Lots of friends, lots of plans, a share house with somebody extra always asleep on the couch, and a fair bit of drama. By the mid-thirties I usually see the attention move to a home. People with this Sun often put real energy into building one around then, a place of their own, a partner, sometimes kids, and the friend group gets smaller and a lot closer. The fifties tend to bring a kind of standing. It's often your place everyone ends up at on a Sunday, and you tend to be the one who keeps the cousins talking to each other after a falling out. The impatience mostly stays. You're still the first to reply in the family group chat, and the first up from the table to start the washing up.

The next time you finish something that took real effort, a job, a move, a hard stretch with your family, mark it before you start the next thing. The catch is that you don't organise it. Ring one person you trust, tell them what you finished, and ask them to pick the place and the time. Turn up, let them pay if they offer, and don't bring up what's next until you're on your way home. You'll probably find it harder than throwing a party for twenty.
